PROBES (builds): `#pragma opt_propagation off` on the line before the definition and `#pragma opt_propagation reset` on the line after the closing brace, applied to fn_80046680, then to move_logic22, then to fn_8004DF58 as the positive control -- each alone, each discarded with `probe.py <unit> <fn> --discard --whole-file` before the next, `git status --short` clean of enemy.c between them.
attributes.residual: THE CORRELATION, BOTH WAYS, AND IT IS FLAT. opt_propagation COVERAGE by definition-order extent, against ADDR16_LO class membership: P (ours pays the surplus copy) 5 of 43 covered = 11.6%; Q-exact (both sides pay equally AND the function is byte-exact -- the positive control corpus) 1 of 30 = 3.3%; Q-fuzzy 2 of 16 = 12.5%; S (the single inverse function) 0 of 1. Four excess covered members out of 43 is not a separation, and the DIRECTION is wrong for the lever besides: opt_propagation off DELETES copies (the fn_8004DF58 control), so if coverage mattered the P members would be UNDER-represented among covered functions, not over. Five P members are covered and still pay the surplus copy -- TriggerCamUpdate, AudioBuildMusicName, AudioSetupBossStreams, check_prefs_loaded, init_mapscreen -- which is a five-instance zero-build counterexample on its own. THE SECOND FINDING IS METHODOLOGICAL AND IS THE ONE THAT TRANSFERS. The PRESENCE screen -- 'does this function's TU contain an opt_propagation pragma anywhere', the question the leak law says is the wrong one -- reports P 32/43 = 74.4% against Q-exact 13/30 = 43.3%, which reads as a strong, publishable signal. The correct EXTENT measure over the identical population collapses it to 11.6% against 3.3%. Same data, same corpus, one wrong question, and a 31-point separation that is an artifact of TU size and pragma-richness rather than of coverage. This is the same failure mode as the run-52 methodology finding that image-wide contrasts manufacture separations, reproduced on a new axis, and it is why al_pragma_extent.py reports BOTH numbers side by side instead of only the one it believes.

hypothesis.cheapest_refuting_observation: `python tools/gdl/composed_census/al_pragma_extent.py` -- if game/sys/memcard's row stops reading `events=1 bare_resets=0 dangling=1 covered_fns=33/35`, the leak is closed or was misread. A `grep -n pragma src/game/sys/memcard.c` returning any `opt_propagation reset` refutes the dangling claim outright.
hypothesis.count_consequence: Unknown and potentially large: opt_propagation changes instruction counts (it cost fn_8004DF58 an `addi`, T316/O315), so closing a region covering 32 functions can move counts across the whole TU and will relocate any downstream webfrank pin window. Treat it as a TU-wide re-measurement, not a one-function edit.
hypothesis.screened_against_target: no -- I do not own game/sys/memcard.c (its webfrank block is claude-fleet-worker-WR's per `claimscope.py --index`) and made no edit there, so whether closing the region improves or regresses those 32 functions is UNMEASURED. The leak's existence is measured; its sign is not.
hypothesis.statement: src/game/sys/memcard.c carries a DANGLING `#pragma opt_propagation off` and 33 of its 35 functions are compiling under it unintentionally. Line 267 opens the region immediately above `int add_vmu_file(...)`, whose preceding comment shows it was meant to bracket that ONE function (a park note describing a base-accumulator web and an in-place shift rotation), and the file contains no `opt_propagation reset` or `on` anywhere -- the only other pragmas are two properly paired `opt_common_subs off`/`reset` regions at 362/431 and 739/906. This is the exact leak EO recorded in enemy.c, in a TU nobody has screened, and memcard also holds a class member (check_prefs_loaded, one of the four remaining shape-V rows). The next lane on memcard should close the region after add_vmu_file's brace and re-measure the TU: the 32 downstream functions are being optimised under an option set nobody chose for them.
